original_value: Enabling haptic communication as well as voice and data over the future 5G cellular system has become a demand. Tactile Internet is one of the main use cases of the 5G system that will allow the transfer of haptic communications in real time. Latency, availability, reliability, and security are the main design challenges of the tactile Internet system and haptic based bilateral teleoperation systems. An end-to-end latency of 1 ms remains the main challenge toward tactile Internet system realization, not only for the processing and coding delays but mainly for the limitations of light. In this work, we analyze the key solutions to overcome the light limitations and enable the tactile Internet over any distances with the required latency. Building a virtual model or model mediated for the remote environment at the edge cloud unit near to the end user is the main solution. By means of AI, the virtual model can predict the behavior of the remote environment and thus, the end user can interact with the virtual environment with a high system experience. This literature review covers the existing work of the model mediated bilateral teleoperated systems and discusses its availability for the tactile Internet system. Furthermore, the security issues of tactile Internet system and the effect of model mediated system on the required security level of tactile Internet applications are discussed. Finally, a structure for the tactile Internet system, with the deployment of model mediation, is suggested.

result.paraphrase: Providing haptic communication alongside voice and data over the future 5G cellular network has become a requirement. One of 5G’s main use cases is the Tactile Internet, which will make real-time haptic communication possible. Latency, availability, reliability, and security are the key design challenges for both tactile Internet systems and haptic-based bilateral teleoperation systems. Achieving 1 ms end-to-end latency remains the primary hurdle for realizing the tactile Internet, due not only to processing and coding delays but especially to the speed-of-light constraint. In this work, we examine the main solutions for overcoming these light-speed limitations and enabling the tactile Internet over any distance with the needed latency. The central approach is to build a virtual or model-mediated representation of the remote environment at an edge-cloud unit close to the end user. Using AI, this virtual model can predict the behavior of the remote environment, allowing the end user to interact with the virtual environment with a high-quality experience. This literature review surveys existing work on model-mediated bilateral teleoperated systems and evaluates their suitability for the tactile Internet system. It also discusses the security concerns of tactile Internet systems and how model-mediated systems affect the security requirements of tactile Internet applications. Finally, it proposes an architecture for the tactile Internet system with model mediation deployment.
